question: To qualify for a Florida real estate broker license, an applicant who holds an active Florida sales associate license must have held that active license for a minimum of how many months during the 5-year period preceding the broker application, effective July 1, 2008?
explanation: Section 475.17(1)(b), F.S., requires an applicant for a broker license to have held an active real estate license (sales associate or broker, in Florida or another state) for at least 24 months during the preceding 5 years.
source_note: Section 475.17, F.S. (broker experience requirement); DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' page

question: A FREC-approved pre-licensing course for brokers consists of how many classroom hours?
explanation: Florida's broker pre-licensing course is a 72-classroom-hour FREC-approved course, distinct from the 63-hour (post-2023) sales associate pre-license course, and remains valid for licensure purposes for two years after completion.
source_note: DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' official page (REBKRequirements.pdf)

question: A candidate's Certificate of Pre-Licensing Education Completion for the broker course remains valid for licensure/testing purposes for how long after the completion date?
explanation: The broker pre-licensing course certificate is valid for two years after the completion date; an expired certificate will not be accepted at the test center even if the candidate's exam authorization is still valid.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet, Admission Procedures section (effective March 2024)

question: What passing grade must a candidate achieve on the Florida Real Estate Broker Examination?
explanation: The DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet confirms the broker exam is graded on a 100-point scale, and a candidate must score 75 points or higher to pass -- a higher bar than the 70-point passing score for the sales associate exam.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet (effective March 2024), 'Scoring Procedures'

question: The Florida Real Estate Broker licensure examination consists of how many multiple-choice questions and how much time is allotted?
explanation: The DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet confirms the broker exam consists of 100 multiple-choice questions with a total of three and a half hours allotted, a closed-book exam administered on computer by Pearson VUE.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet (effective March 2024), 'The Examination'

question: A licensed Florida sales associate who has satisfied the 24-month active-license experience requirement and wants to become a broker must, before being eligible, also have:
choice_a: Held a broker's license in another state for at least 5 years
choice_b: Successfully completed the sales associate post-licensing education requirement
choice_c: Completed the broker post-licensing course before taking the broker exam
choice_d: No additional requirement beyond the 24 months of licensure
explanation: DBPR's official broker requirements page notes that a Florida sales associate applying for a broker license must first fulfill the sales associate post-licensing education requirement; the broker-pathway experience credit does not exempt the sales associate from that separate obligation.
source_note: DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' official page (REBKRequirements.pdf), Note under item 1

question: After passing the broker exam and being issued a license, a new broker must complete a FREC-approved post-licensing course for brokers before the initial license expires. How many classroom hours must that course consist of?
explanation: Florida requires a new broker to complete a FREC-approved post-licensing course of at least 60 classroom hours before the initial broker license expires; failure to do so results in the license reverting to a null-and-void status requiring the licensee to requalify.
source_note: DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' official page (REBKRequirements.pdf), item 6

question: Once initial post-licensing education has been satisfied, how many hours of continuing education (CE) must a broker complete each 2-year license renewal period?
explanation: After the initial post-licensing course, Florida brokers and broker associates must complete 14 hours of FREC-approved continuing education every two-year renewal cycle to keep the license active.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Commission Licensure Information page

question: To submit a completed DBPR RE 13 Broker Transactions form is necessary for what purpose?
choice_a: To activate a newly issued broker license, since otherwise it is issued in an inactive status
choice_b: To register a new brokerage entity's fictitious name
choice_c: To renew a sales associate license
choice_d: To request a mutual recognition license
explanation: A new broker license is issued in inactive status by default; the DBPR RE 13 Broker Transactions form must be submitted to activate the license (e.g., to operate as a sole proprietor broker or register with a brokerage entity).
source_note: DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' official page (REBKRequirements.pdf), item 5

question: A licensee applying for a Florida broker license based on out-of-state real estate experience must attach to the application:
choice_a: A letter of recommendation from a Florida-licensed broker
choice_b: A current certification of real estate license history from the other jurisdiction's licensing agency, not more than 30 days old
choice_c: Proof of at least 5 years of continuous residency in that other state
choice_d: Nothing beyond the standard application, since out-of-state experience is never accepted
explanation: An applicant claiming experience from a jurisdiction other than Florida must attach a current certification of real estate license history (issued within 30 days of application) from that jurisdiction's licensing agency, confirming at least 24 months of active licensure within the preceding 5 years obtained through that state's own education and examination requirements.
source_note: DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' official page (REBKRequirements.pdf), item 1

question: Florida's mutual recognition agreements, allowing certain licensees from other states to bypass the standard 72-hour prelicensing coursework and instead pass a Florida-specific law exam, currently extend to license holders from how many states?
explanation: DBPR's official Mutual Recognition States page lists 10 states with current mutual recognition agreements with Florida: Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Georgia, Illinois, Kentucky, Mississippi, Nebraska, Rhode Island, and West Virginia.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Commission 'Mutual Recognition States' official page

question: Under Florida's mutual recognition framework, a qualifying non-resident licensee from a mutual recognition state is nevertheless required to:
choice_a: Complete the full 72-hour Florida broker pre-license course anyway
choice_b: Reside in Florida for at least one year before applying
choice_c: Obtain sponsorship from a Florida-licensed broker before applying
choice_d: Pass a Florida-specific real estate law examination
explanation: Mutual recognition lets an eligible out-of-state licensee skip Florida's standard prelicensing coursework, but the applicant must still pass a Florida-specific law examination covering Florida license law and rules before a Florida license is issued.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Commission 'Mutual Recognition States' official page; F.A.C. 61J2-26

question: An applicant with a permanent physical disability under FREC Rule 61J2-3.013(2) who is unable to attend the site where a broker prelicensing course is conducted may qualify for:
choice_b: A full exemption from all prelicensing education
choice_c: An automatic waiver of the licensing exam
choice_d: A reduced course requirement of 36 hours
explanation: FREC Rule 61J2-3.013(2) allows an applicant with a qualifying permanent physical disability who cannot physically attend the classroom site to complete an approved correspondence prelicensing course instead.
source_note: F.A.C. 61J2-3.013(2); DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' official page (REBKRequirements.pdf), item 2

question: In addition to the completed application and applicable fee, a Florida real estate broker applicant must also submit:
choice_c: Proof of errors and omissions insurance
explanation: Florida broker applicants must submit electronic fingerprints as part of the background screening process required alongside the completed application and fee.
source_note: DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Requirements' official page (REBKRequirements.pdf), item 3

question: A broker who wishes to hold licenses at more than one brokerage location under a single license, rather than obtain a separate license for each additional location, should understand the distinction between:
choice_c: Multiple licenses versus a group license
explanation: FREC's licensing framework distinguishes between holding multiple individual licenses at different brokerages versus a group license arrangement, a topic the Broker Content Outline expressly lists under Licensure Requirements.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet, Content Overview and Outline, Section I.A.10

question: If a Florida real estate broker changes their business or mailing address, they are required to:
choice_a: Take no action unless the change also involves a name change
choice_c: Wait until the next renewal cycle to report it
choice_d: Notify DBPR of the change of address
explanation: A Florida broker must promptly notify DBPR of any change of address; this is listed as a distinct licensure requirement topic on the broker exam content outline and can be completed online through DBPR's licensee services.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet, Content Overview and Outline, Section I.A.11

question: Which of the following is generally recognized under Florida law as an exemption from real estate licensure requirements?
choice_a: An attorney-at-law performing services within the scope of the attorney-client relationship
choice_b: A property management company handling rentals for a fee with no license at all
choice_c: Any unlicensed assistant negotiating a sales price on the broker's behalf
choice_d: A for-sale-by-owner seller's unlicensed friend handling all offers for a commission
explanation: Section 475.011, F.S., lists categories exempt from real estate licensure requirements, including attorneys-at-law acting within an attorney-client relationship; unlicensed persons generally may not negotiate real estate transactions or receive compensation for doing so.
source_note: Section 475.011, F.S. (Exemptions); DBPR Real Estate Broker Candidate Information Booklet, Content Overview and Outline, Section I.A.12

question: An applicant for a Florida real estate broker license must be at least how old and possess what identifying credential?
choice_b: 18 years old, with a Social Security number
choice_c: 18 years old, with a state-issued driver's license only
choice_d: 25 years old, with a college degree
explanation: Florida requires real estate license applicants, including broker applicants, to be at least 18 years old and to hold a Social Security number as part of the application's identification requirements.
source_note: Section 475.17, F.S.; DBPR licensing guidance summarized on the Real Estate Commission Licensure Information page
